faq.a: Azize is associated with the Arabic form عَزِيزَة, whose core sense is azize; dear, mighty (feminine).

faq.q: What is the origin of Azize?
faq.a: Azize is associated with Arabic. Azize is the Turkish form of Arabic عَزِيزَة (ʿAzīza), the feminine of عَزِيز, meaning 'dear, mighty'.
Yes — the underlying form عَزِيزَة is Arabic.
Azize can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Azize should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ع ز ز is Quranic, but ʿAzīza is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Azize mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Azize is rendered عزیزہ and carries the sense عزیزہ، پیاری.

faq.q: What does Azize mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Azize is rendered عزیزه and carries the sense عزیزه، عزیز.
A romanized syllable approximation is a-zi-ze. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Azize?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Azize, azize. Script forms are عزيزه, عزیزه, عزیزہ, عَزِيزَة, अज़ीज़ा.

faq.q: Is Azize a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
